When the react app is connected to the electron app through a websocket, we don't correctly handle the commands 'copy path' an 'copy relative path': they give an error.

this is not correct: we should still allow to copy the path and relative path.

## Current state

* `CardPathMenuItems` (`app/src/components/card_view/card_path_menu_items.tsx`) renders `Copy path` and `Copy relative path` for card tiles (`project_card_view.tsx`) and file-tree card rows (`file_tree_node_row.tsx`). Its `copyCardPath` helper calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText` directly and reports any throw through `dialogService.error` with fallback message `Path could not be copied to clipboard`.
* Remote control means: the React app runs in a browser on another device and reaches the Electron host over a WebSocket, proxied by `RemoteControlStorageService`. The host serves that page over plain HTTP at `http://host:port/` (`buildRemoteConnectUrl`, `app/src/data/remote_connect_string.ts`).
* A page served over plain HTTP from a non-`localhost` host is not a *secure context*, so the browser does not expose the async Clipboard API: `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`. Reading `.writeText` on it throws a `TypeError` before any copy is attempted, the `catch` fires, and the user sees the copy error dialog instead of a copied path. This is the reported failure, and it hits both menu items.
* In remote-control mode the project reference is proxied whole from the host, so `project.rootPath` is present and points at the host machine's repository directory. Both menu items therefore render remotely; only the clipboard write fails. Remote *GitHub-storage* projects still have no `rootPath` and keep showing only `Copy relative path`, per F\_116.
* A working non-secure-context fallback already exists in the codebase: `copyText` in `app/src/components/shell/remote_control_connection_info.tsx` writes through a temporary hidden `textarea` plus the legacy `document.execCommand('copy')`, which browsers still allow inside a user-gesture handler on insecure origins.

## implementation details

* Extract the clipboard write into one shared renderer helper, `app/src/services/clipboard_text.ts`, exporting an async `copyTextToClipboard(text: string): Promise<void>` that resolves on success and rejects with an `Error` when neither path works.
* Order inside the helper: use `navigator.clipboard.writeText` when `navigator.clipboard` exists; otherwise, or when that call rejects, fall back to the `textarea` + `document.execCommand('copy')` path. Guard the property access so a missing `navigator.clipboard` selects the fallback instead of throwing.
* In the fallback, append the `textarea` to `document.body`, select its content, run `document.execCommand('copy')`, and remove the element in a `finally` so no stray node survives a throw. `document.execCommand` returns `false` when the browser refuses the copy; treat `false` as failure and reject, so the user still gets the existing error dialog rather than silent nothing.
* Point `copyCardPath` in `card_path_menu_items.tsx` at the helper, keeping the current behaviour around it unchanged: close the menu first via `onSelected()`, then write, then report failure through `dialogService.error` with the same `Path could not be copied to clipboard` fallback message. Copied values stay exactly as F\_116 defines them.
* Replace the private `copyText` in `remote_control_connection_info.tsx` with the shared helper so both call sites behave identically. That component currently swallows fallback failures; keep its existing behaviour by catching the rejection there, so the Serve popover's copy button does not start raising new dialogs.
* Renderer-only change. No Electron bridge, no WebSocket message, no persistence, no Git operation, no card or project state change.
* Tests: unit-test the helper for the secure path, the missing-`navigator.clipboard` path, the rejected-`writeText` path, the `execCommand` returning `false` path, and `textarea` cleanup. Extend `card_path_menu_items.grouped.test.tsx` with a remote-style case where `navigator.clipboard` is absent and the copy still succeeds through the fallback with no error dialog.

## acceptance criteria

* With the app served over plain HTTP from a remote host (no `navigator.clipboard`), choosing `Copy relative path` on a card writes the unchanged repository-relative path, for example `design/F_116.md`, and shows no error dialog.
* In that same remote session, choosing `Copy path` writes the host-machine absolute path built from the proxied `project.rootPath`, using the host root's separators, and shows no error dialog.
* In a normal secure-context desktop session, both items keep using the async Clipboard API and produce the values already required by F\_116.
* When both the Clipboard API and the `execCommand` fallback fail, the user sees the existing `Path could not be copied to clipboard` error, and no card, project, or repository state changes.
* Both items still close their menu before the clipboard write, from card tiles and file-tree card rows, whether opened by right-click or the three-dot button.
* The Serve popover's connect-URL copy button keeps working on insecure origins and keeps silently ignoring a failed copy.
* No temporary `textarea` remains in the DOM after a successful or failed fallback copy.

## Finding: why grouped tests are excluded

Traced it. Commit `ecb2f137` ("Integrate into project", 2026-08-31) did two things in one go: renamed ~73 component test files from `*.test.tsx` to `*.grouped.test.tsx`, and added `src/**/*.grouped.test.tsx` to the `exclude` list of the `ui` project in `app/vite.config.ts:156`. It never added a project that *includes* that pattern. No commit anywhere in history adds one.

So the exclusion has a purpose — carving heavy jsdom component tests out of the default `vitest run` — but the other half of the refactor is missing. Result today: all 73 grouped files run in **no** vitest project. `npm run test -- <grouped file>` matches nothing.

Earlier feature docs confirm how agents coped: `B_224` lists `app/vite.grouped.config.ts` and `F_270` lists `app/vitest.grouped.temp.config.ts` in their `affects` — throwaway configs created to run them, then deleted. I reproduced that: a temp config does load them, but they fail on setup (`ConfigService.init` via `mergeStoredReactValues`) because the base `setupFiles` alone isn't what they were written against. I removed my temp config again; worktree is clean of it.

So a `.grouped.test.tsx` file written today is unrunnable and unverifiable. Fixing that properly is its own job, outside F_337.

## Recommendation

Write the new-card-dialog test as `new_card_dialog_back_dismiss.test.tsx` (plain suffix, runs in the `ui` project). Same content the spec asks for, only the file suffix deviates, and I can actually prove the acceptance criteria pass.

## Change plan — 4 blocks

**Block 1 — back-dismiss service**
`app/src/services/mobile_back_dismiss_service.ts`, new. Class `MobileBackDismissService` plus singleton `mobileBackDismissService` registered through `register()`. Holds an ordered registration array of `{ id, onDismiss }`, attaches the single `popstate` listener lazily on first `register()` so the constructor never touches `window` (node tests stub `window` as `{}`).
- `register(id, onDismiss)` pushes `history.pushState({ md2BackDismiss: id }, '')` with no URL argument, then appends the record.
- `popstate` handler: if the self-inflicted counter is above zero it decrements and returns; else, if the array is empty it returns; else it calls the top `onDismiss()` and synchronously pushes a replacement entry. It does not drop the registration.
- `unregister(id)` removes the record and increments a queued-unwind counter, flushed once per microtask as one `history.go(-count)`, incrementing the self-inflicted counter by one per `go()` call (one `go` produces one `popstate`, not `count` of them).
Test: `mobile_back_dismiss_service.node.test.ts` with a fake window (EventTarget + history stub) covering push-on-register, top dismissal plus replacement push, ignored `popstate` when nothing is registered, several unregistrations batched into one `history.go(-n)`, and no dismissal firing on a self-inflicted unwind.

**Block 2 — card popup wiring**
`app/src/components/hooks/use_card_popup_back_dismiss.ts`, new. Subscribes via `subscribeCardPopups`, computes `active = isMobile && !isElectron()`, keeps the registration count equal to `entries.length` when active and zero otherwise, and unregisters everything on unmount. Dismiss callback reads the live snapshot and calls `cardPopupService.close(entries.at(-1).id)`. Mounted once in `app/src/components/project_workspace.tsx`, which is the single owner of both `CardActionPopupHost` and (through `CardView`/`MobileCardView`) `CardBodyPopover`.
Test: `use_card_popup_back_dismiss.test.tsx` covering two stacked popups needing two back presses, and desktop-width or Electron registering nothing.

**Block 3 — new-card dialog**
`app/src/components/shell/project/new_card_dialog.tsx`: effect registering while `open && isMobile && !isElectron()`, dismiss callback delegating to `handleDialogClose` through a ref so the effect doesn't re-run per render. Unregister on close/unmount.
Test: `new_card_dialog_back_dismiss.test.tsx` covering back with a clean draft closing the dialog, and back with a dirty draft showing the discard confirmation while the dialog stays open.

**Block 4 — status**
Set `status: ready` in `design/feature_descriptions/F_337_handle_back_button_when_on_mobile.md`.

No Electron main-process, preload, WebSocket, persistence or Git changes. I'll run only the three new test files plus `npm run typecheck`.

Approve the plan, and confirm the plain-`.test.tsx` choice for Block 3?

## Answer: the exclusion is load-bearing, and grouped tests do run

I was wrong in my previous message — correcting that. Grouped tests are not orphaned.

The mechanism: alongside each set of `*.grouped.test.tsx` files sits an aggregator named `*_no_mock.test.tsx` that does nothing but import them:

```
app/src/components/shell/project/new_card_no_mock.test.tsx
    import './new_card_dialog_attachment.grouped.test'
    import './new_card_markdown_editor.grouped.test'
```

There are 9 such aggregators, and every one of the 73 grouped files is imported by exactly one of them — I checked all 73, none is orphaned. The aggregator is a plain `.test.tsx`, so the `ui` project collects it and runs its imported suites. The `exclude` line at `app/vite.config.ts:156` exists precisely so vitest does not *also* collect each grouped file standalone, which would run every one of those suites twice.

Purpose of the grouping, from the naming and the contents: a `_no_mock` file batches many component suites into one jsdom module registry, so they pay the module-graph and environment cost once instead of 73 times. That only works if the batched suites don't call `vi.mock`, since a module mock in one would leak into its file-mates — and indeed only 2 of the 73 use `vi.mock` at all. Same commit `ecb2f137` flipped `fileParallelism` to `true` and `TEST_WORKERS` from 1 to 2, so this was a test-speed refactor.

Verified live: `npm run test -- src/components/shell/project/new_card_no_mock.test.tsx` passes, running both grouped suites it imports. My earlier temp-config failures were my config's fault, not the tests'.

So the spec's instruction is right as written, and the question I asked you is moot. Block 3 gets a real `.grouped.test.tsx`, registered in the existing aggregator, and written without `vi.mock`.

## Change plan — 4 blocks

**Block 1 — back-dismiss service**
New `app/src/services/mobile_back_dismiss_service.ts`: class `MobileBackDismissService` plus singleton `mobileBackDismissService` via `register()`. Ordered array of `{ id, onDismiss }`; the single `popstate` listener attaches lazily on the first `register()` so the constructor never touches `window` (node tests stub `window` as `{}`).
- `register(id, onDismiss)` calls `history.pushState({ md2BackDismiss: id }, '')` with no URL argument, then appends the record.
- The `popstate` handler returns early after decrementing the self-inflicted counter when that counter is above zero; returns when the array is empty; otherwise calls the top `onDismiss()` and synchronously pushes a replacement entry, keeping the registration.
- `unregister(id)` removes the record and increments a queued-unwind counter that a microtask flushes once as `history.go(-count)`, raising the self-inflicted counter by one per `go()` call, because one `go(-n)` produces one `popstate`, not n.

Test `mobile_back_dismiss_service.node.test.ts` with a fake window (EventTarget plus history stub): push on register, top dismissal with replacement push, ignored `popstate` when nothing is registered, several unregistrations batched into one `history.go`, and no dismissal on a self-inflicted unwind.

**Block 2 — card popup wiring**
New `app/src/components/hooks/use_card_popup_back_dismiss.ts`: subscribes through `subscribeCardPopups`, computes `active = isMobile && !isElectron()`, keeps the registration count equal to `entries.length` when active and zero otherwise, unregisters all on unmount. Dismiss callback reads the live snapshot and calls `cardPopupService.close(entries.at(-1).id)`. Called once from `app/src/components/project_workspace.tsx`, the single owner of both `CardActionPopupHost` and, through `CardView`/`MobileCardView`, `CardBodyPopover`.
Test `use_card_popup_back_dismiss.test.tsx` (plain, so it may mock `isElectron`): two stacked popups need two back presses; desktop width or Electron registers nothing.

**Block 3 — new-card dialog**
`new_card_dialog.tsx` gains an effect registering while `open && isMobile && !isElectron()`, its dismiss callback delegating to `handleDialogClose` through a ref so the effect does not re-run each render; unregisters on close and unmount.
Test `new_card_dialog_back_dismiss.grouped.test.tsx`, no `vi.mock`, added as an import to `new_card_no_mock.test.tsx`: back with a clean draft closes the dialog; back with a dirty draft shows the discard confirmation and the dialog stays open. Electron detection there is steered by assigning `window.md2Lifecycle` rather than mocking the module, which keeps the file mock-free.

F_337 done, status set to `ready`.

**What was built**

`app/src/services/mobile_back_dismiss_service.ts` — the single owner of back-button dismissal. Each `register(id, onDismiss)` pushes one history entry via `history.pushState({ md2BackDismiss: id }, '')` with no URL argument, so the hash never changes and `useAppLocation` stays on its route. A `popstate` calls the top registration's `onDismiss` and immediately pushes a replacement, keeping the registration alive because a dismissal is a request, not a guaranteed close. `unregister` queues one unwind step; a microtask flushes them as a single `history.go(-count)`, and a self-inflicted counter makes the service ignore the `popstate` that its own move produces. It is the only place in the app that calls `pushState`.

`app/src/components/hooks/use_card_popup_back_dismiss.ts` — keeps the registration count equal to the number of open card popups whenever `isMobile && !isElectron()`, dismissing by `cardPopupService.close(entries.at(-1).id)`. Mounted once from `project_workspace.tsx:100`, which owns both `CardActionPopupHost` and, through `CardView`/`MobileCardView`, `CardBodyPopover`. Takes an optional service argument, following the `useWorkspaceView(service = …)` convention, which is what makes it testable without module resets.

`new_card_dialog.tsx` — registers while `open && isMobile && !isElectron()`, dismissing through `handleDialogClose`, so back behaves exactly like the close button: clean draft closes, dirty draft opens the discard confirmation and the dialog stays open, and a second back press hits the existing `dismissalPhaseRef` guard.

**Tests** — 7 node tests for the service, 4 component tests for the hook, 3 grouped tests for the dialog registered in `new_card_no_mock.test.tsx`. All pass, together with the neighbouring `project_dialogs`, `new_card_dialog_render` and `test:related` suites for the two changed components (95 tests). `npm run typecheck` and eslint on all touched files are clean.

**Two things worth knowing**

The test stubs for `history.go` must dispatch a `popstate` the way a real browser does. Without that the service's self-inflicted counter never drains and the next back press is silently swallowed — that is real behaviour the tests now pin, not a test workaround.

This repo has no React Testing Library auto-cleanup, since vitest `globals` is off. A test that renders must call `cleanup()` itself, otherwise the previous test's component stays mounted and keeps reacting to service events. Both new component test files do this, matching `use_active_card.test.tsx`.
